title: Extracting Boundary Conformal Data from Periodic Non-Hermitian Critical Chains
authors: Yifan Liu, Haruki Shimizu, Dongchang Liu, Kohei Kawabata
abstract: Boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) contains universal data that are usually accessed microscopically by imposing spatial boundaries on the lattice. Here, we introduce a periodic-chain projected-partition-function spectroscopy that extracts universal boundary quantities directly from non-Hermitian bulk-critical quantum chains, avoiding the need to engineer microscopic open boundaries and circumventing subtle boundary effects in non-Hermitian systems. Using a short-range-entangled boundary preparation and its infrared-compatible left dual, we obtain the Affleck-Ludwig boundary entropy in non-Hermitian systems. We demonstrate this construction for two representative non-Hermitian infrared structures. For a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Ising realization of the real nonunitary Yang-Lee CFT, we extract the minimal-boundary projected coefficient and recover a nontrivial negative excited-to-ground ratio. For the genuinely complex fixed points of the non-Hermitian five-state Potts chain, we resolve intrinsically complex boundary coefficients and reproduce the exact relation required by the Kramers-Wannier duality. Our results establish a route to nonunitary BCFT universal data via only knowledge of the bulk critical system, opening a window into non-Hermitian boundary criticality.
summary: The paper presents a novel spectroscopic technique to extract Boundary Conformal Field Theory (BCFT) data directly from periodic, non-Hermitian critical chains. By analyzing projected partition functions and their ratios, the authors successfully recover universal boundary quantities for models like the Yang–Lee CFT and the Potts chain without needing explicit open boundary engineering. This establishes a general theoretical route into non-unitary boundary criticality using only bulk information.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing a method to extract universal Boundary Conformal Field Theory (BCFT) data from non-Hermitian bulk-critical quantum chains.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated the extraction of boundary data for both $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Ising models and the five-state Potts chain, confirming relations like Kramers–Wannier duality using only knowledge of the periodic bulk system.
method: They introduce 'projected-partition-function spectroscopy' by analyzing the scaling limit of projected amplitudes $Z_{\Phi,i}(L)$ to extract boundary coefficients while circumventing engineered open boundaries.
model_or_system: The work applies to non-Hermitian quantum many-body systems exhibiting critical phenomena, specifically tested on a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Ising realization of the Yang–Lee CFT and the five-state Potts chain.
key_observables: Universal boundary-state coefficients ($G_a(\Phi),i$), boundary entropy (Affleck–Ludwig $g$-factor), and ratios of projected partition functions, such as $	ext{R}_{\Phi,1}(L)$.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the thermodynamic limit ($L 	o \infty$) and involves analyzing finite-size scaling corrections based on irrelevant operators.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that a short-range preparation state can microscopically represent a conformal boundary condition, allowing nonuniversal terms to be canceled via ratios or scaling analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the finite-size extraction of Yang–Lee boundary coefficients and complex Potts projected coefficients ($g_k$) versus $1/L$, comparing numerical results against established BCFT predictions.
paper_structure: The paper develops from defining the projected amplitude, establishing its scaling behavior using ratios to eliminate nonuniversal factors, and then applying this robust framework sequentially to two distinct physical realizations (Yang-Lee CFT and Potts chain) to validate its applicability across different boundary regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, purely bulk-based theoretical tool for accessing universal boundary physics in complex, non-Hermitian quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding open or engineered quantum boundaries.
